b2-uruguay-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why the Schools Are Free
b2-uruguay-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Uruguay, and he asks why public school there is free.
b2-uruguay-01.prompt: Tell Carlos the reason, with a cause connector.
cues: Say that public school is free and compulsory
b2-uruguay-01.target: A raíz de la reforma de Varela, la escuela pública es gratuita y obligatoria.
b2-uruguay-01.english: As a result of Varela's reform, public school is free and compulsory.
b2-uruguay-01.canDo: I can give reasons for the reforms of the 1900s with *debido a* and *a raíz de*.

b2-uruguay-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Candombe and UNESCO
b2-uruguay-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You have read an article about candombe, and Meg asks what UNESCO did in 2009.
b2-uruguay-02.prompt: Tell Meg what UNESCO did and what it was for.
cues: Say that UNESCO included candombe in its list
Say what it was for, with a purpose phrase
b2-uruguay-02.target: La UNESCO incluyó el candombe en su lista con el fin de ayudar a protegerlo.
b2-uruguay-02.english: UNESCO included candombe in its list in order to help protect it.
b2-uruguay-02.canDo: I can say what a tradition or a decision is for with *con miras a* and *con el fin de*.

b2-uruguay-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Plebiscite of 1980
b2-uruguay-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are giving a short talk about Uruguay, and Carlos asks what happened in 1980.
b2-uruguay-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what the military wanted and what the result was.
cues: Say what the military wanted to approve and how
b2-uruguay-03.target: Los militares quisieron aprobar una Constitución mediante un plebiscito, pero ganó el «No».
b2-uruguay-03.english: The military wanted to approve a constitution by means of a plebiscite, but the "No" won.
b2-uruguay-03.canDo: I can say how something was done in politics with *mediante*.

b2-uruguay-04.title: Communicative Challenge: The Plan Ceibal
b2-uruguay-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Uruguay's schools, and she asks how the Plan Ceibal changed over time.
b2-uruguay-04.prompt: Tell Meg what the plan went on to include.
cues: Say that the plan changed with time
Say that it went on to include secondary students
b2-uruguay-04.target: Con el tiempo, el Plan Ceibal pasó a incluir a los alumnos de secundaria.
b2-uruguay-04.english: In time, the Plan Ceibal went on to include secondary students.
b2-uruguay-04.canDo: I can say what a policy went on to include with *pasar a* + infinitive.

b2-uruguay-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Mate in Montevideo
b2-uruguay-05.scenario: You are Meg. You watched a documentary about Montevideo, and Carlos asks what struck you.
b2-uruguay-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you noticed about the mate.
b2-uruguay-05.target: Me di cuenta de que muchos uruguayos llevan un termo bajo el brazo.
b2-uruguay-05.english: I realised that many Uruguayans carry a thermos under their arm.
b2-uruguay-05.canDo: I can describe getting used to life in Montevideo with *acostumbrarse a* and *darse cuenta de*.

b2-uruguay-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Uruguay in Brief
b2-uruguay-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You are preparing a short talk about Uruguay, and Meg asks you to try one sentence about 1980.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how Uruguayans rejected the military's constitution.
cues: Say how it was done, with a formal phrase
b2-uruguay-consolidation.target: En 1980, mediante un plebiscito, los uruguayos rechazaron la Constitución propuesta por los militares.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.english: In 1980, by means of a plebiscite, Uruguayans rejected the constitution proposed by the military.
b2-uruguay-consolidation.canDo: I can say how something was done in politics with *mediante*.
